display.purpose: Homepage mood sentence only — the single largest statement on the site.

stat.purpose: The giant abnormal-return / ticker figure on why-this-stock pages. Numbers only.

body.purpose: All reading copy — explanations, Q&A, evidence notes.

shadows.name: quiz-option-rest
shadows.purpose: Tactile game-button shadow on homepage quiz answers, at rest.

shadows.name: quiz-option-pressed
shadows.purpose: Quiz answer shadow collapses on :active, giving a physical press feel.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Impact-map line-draw and default state transitions.

components.name: Primary Button (CTA)
components.description: The one primary action on a card, e.g. "อ่านเรื่องนี้ใน 1 นาที".
components.html: อ่านเรื่องนี้ใน 1 นาที
components.css: .ds-cta { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 50px; border-radius: 14px; background: #1B2A4A; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; text-decoration: none; padding: 0 20px; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-cta:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-cta:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #6B4EFF; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px; }

components.name: Line Chip (toggle)
components.description: Selects which market line (oil/inflation/dollar) the impact map highlights.
components.css: .ds-chip { min-height: 40px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1.5px solid #D5DBE3; background: transparent; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; color: #0F1B2D; } .ds-chip i { width: 14px; height: 6px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--lc); } .ds-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--lc); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--lc) 12%, transparent); }

components.name: Exposure Pill
components.description: Marks Positive / Negative / Mixed Exposure. Color and stroke style both carry the signal.
components.css: .ds-pill { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 999px; white-space: nowrap; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; } .ds-pill-pos { color: #15803D; } .ds-pill-neg { color: #C8261E; } .ds-pill-mix { color: #A16207; border-style: dashed; }

components.name: Card (surface container)
components.description: The standard Paper-on-Chalk container used for the impact map, FAQ rows, confidence block, etc.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #D5DBE3; border-radius: 20px; padding: 20px 18px; color: #0F1B2D; }

components.name: Evidence Mark (Fact/Analysis/Uncertainty)
components.description: Three fixed shapes that must never be redrawn differently: filled dot = Fact, hollow ring = Analysis, dashed ring = Uncertainty.
components.css: .ds-mk { width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; display: inline-block; } .ds-mk-f { background: #0F1B2D; } .ds-mk-a { border: 3px solid #0F1B2D; } .ds-mk-u { border: 3px dashed #A16207; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Search box on the stock-search page.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" placeholder="ค้นหา ticker หรือชื่อบริษัท" />
components.css: .ds-input { min-height: 52px; border-radius: 16px; border: 1.5px solid #D5DBE3; padding: 0 16px; font-size: 16px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #0F1B2D; width: 100%; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #6B4EFF; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.northStar: The Transit Map of Cause and Effect
narrative.overview:
The whole system reads as a subway map for market reasoning: a market story is a colored "line" (oil, inflation, dollar) running through fixed "stations" — event → economy → industry → company — and every station is either a solid stop (strong evidence) or a dashed one (a factor that could change the outcome). This is not a decorative metaphor; it is the actual information architecture, so the visual language exists to make cause-and-effect legible at a glance, not to look impressive.

The product is explicitly not a news site and never recommends buying or selling, so the surface stays calm and editorial rather than urgent or salesy: chalk-and-ink neutrals carry almost the whole UI, the three line colors are reserved for their one job, and green/red/amber are reserved for Positive/Negative/Mixed Exposure and nothing else. Corners are soft and forgiving everywhere, borders do the separating work instead of shadows, and the one place the system allows itself to feel playful — the homepage's XP/streak/quiz "learning path" — is deliberately fenced off from the serious reading surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Mobile-first single column (460px, 560px ≥900px), never a wide desktop layout
Flat and bordered by default; shadows appear only in the gamified quiz interaction
One reserved color per market line, never reused for anything else
Fact / Analysis / Uncertainty rendered as three distinct mark shapes, not just three colors
Chakra Petch for anything numeric or declarative; Anuphan for everything read at length

rules.name: The One Job Per Color Rule
rules.body: A line color marks which market story something belongs to and nothing else; an exposure color marks Positive/Negative/Mixed and nothing else.

rules.name: The Dark Mode Mirror Rule
rules.body: Every token has a confirmed dark-mode counterpart via :root[data-theme="dark"] / prefers-color-scheme, not an afterthought filter.

rules.name: The Numbers-Wear-Chakra Rule
rules.body: Any rendered market figure uses Chakra Petch, even inline inside an Anuphan sentence.

rules.name: The Flat-Reading, Tactile-Play Rule
rules.body: Event/evidence/search/calendar stay flat (borders only); shadows are permitted only inside the homepage quiz.

dos: Do keep a line color meaning "this belongs to the oil/inflation/dollar story" everywhere except the tab bar's single active-state exception.
Do pair every exposure color with its stroke-style twin (solid/dashed) so the signal survives grayscale or color-blindness.
Do set every rendered number in Chakra Petch, even mid-sentence.
Do keep event/evidence/search/calendar surfaces flat; reserve shadow for the homepage quiz.
donts: Don't introduce a new accent color outside the three line colors and three exposure colors.
Don't use green/red/amber for anything other than Positive/Negative/Mixed Exposure, even decoratively.
Don't add shadows to a reading surface — that vocabulary belongs to the gamified homepage only.
Don't use a sharp corner anywhere in the system.
Don't widen the core content column into a conventional multi-column desktop layout.
